description: INVERTED by issue #839 (maintainer ruling #833 rule 3, "nothing shadows"). The program is unchanged — `define forward … print 1 … end` then `print fd` — but its outcome is not. Issue #787 authored this as the NO-OUTPUT half of a host-crash regression: a reporter-position Heritage alias over a user procedure that never reaches `return` had to report `ol-no-output` with `params.procedure` carrying the canonical `"forward"`, a DIFFERENT param name from the arity siblings' `params.callable`, so that asserting one did not leave the other unpinned. It was marked TRANSITIONAL when it landed, because it needs a user procedure registered under a Heritage alias's canonical name and every one of the thirteen canonicals is a built-in name. #839's runtime phase-1 registration guard (`spec/execution-model.md:82-89`) now raises `ol-reserved-word` (`spec/error-model.md:125`) at the declaration, so the procedure never runs: the previously non-empty event stream (`procedure-enter`, its own `print 1`, `procedure-exit`) is now empty, which is itself the strongest evidence the halt happens at registration rather than at the reporter position. Kept and inverted rather than deleted, so re-legalising `define forward` reddens this and leads the next reader to #787. The evaluator-level invariant is carried forward in `packages/runtime/src/heritage-alias-chokepoint.test.mjs`.

diagnostics.message: forward is already part of OpenLogo. choose another name.
